Therapy dogs help heal

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Abused and traumatised, many young children fear the day day they have to face their abuser in court, but in a unique program our furry friends are there to help

Unique Selling Point:
Many young victims of abuse fear the day that they have to face the perpetrator in court. But a unique programme involving therapy dogs helps to m ake this daunting task a lot easier.

Summary:
There is a significant lack of specialised services for of sexuall offences in SA. This is despite the enactment of legislation and blueprints that aimto ensure that victims receive effective services from the criminal Justice System role-payers. There can be effective and sensitive services provided these role-players are adequately and consistently trained . Difficulties arise when court officials do not have the specialised knowledge to deal with cases involve in sexual abuse.
Children occupy a special role within human rights protection since they are perceived to require special protection because of their fragile state of development and the fact that they are very susceptible to abuse and neglect and are not in a position to defend themselves. Contemporary research indicates that child victims/witnesses struggle with a number of difficulties in theit interaction with the criminal justice system, which has been attributed to their lack of maturity and developmental shortages.There has been a growing concern about the effects on children of giving evidence in an adversarial environment. Many claim that court involvement traumatises a child victim. Not only does confrontation with the accused cause trauma for the child witnesses. Cross-examination is not only traumatic for children, but also results in inaccurate evidence. The child is questioned in a hostile environment, often about ery intimate and emotionally laden events.

SCRIPT Therapy Dogs



PROMO 1 11”
Abused and traumatized, many young children fear the day day they have to face their abuser in court, But in a unique program our furry friends are there to help
PROMO 2 11”
Having to testify in court and facing the harsh reality of the law is a traumatic experience young victims of crime.Therapy dogs help ease them in the daunting process.
PROMO 3 11”
What seems like a fun play day with man/s best friend, is actually a court preparation program, helping abused children to become credible witnesses , when the day comes to testify in court.






Court scenes
All rise --- court scenes


Link Claire







Claire V/O
15”






Shaheda Omar







Claire V/O
13”









Shaheda Omar








Claire V/O
4”



Claire Question


Belinda Lamb
Group Leader: Top Dogs







This isn't just a day of fun and laughter. What you’ve just seen is part of a crucial process to prepare children for possibly one of the most challenging days of their lives - testifying in court.
_________________________________

Meet Shiloh, she is the magistrate in court today, , Shadow , the court orderly , Yazzi, the prosecutor, Zoe the defence lawyer and Cadbury the defendant. They are some of the dogs that passed the assessment process for this volunteer program
_________________________
11:57 This is ground breaking, we are change makers, where dogs are actually dressed in uniforms of the court personnel and children are given the opportunity to identify with the respective members in the courtroom and their roles and responsibilities
_________________________________
Dr Shaheda Omar is the director of the Teddy Bear Clinic, spearheading the dog therapy program preparing young victims of crime for their day in court and helping to allay fears of the Criminal Justice system



00:32
Historically, if we look at disadvantaged population groups, there is an enormous fear an immense fear of Police Officers and dogs.
With the dogs we have actually tried to break down the stereotype that not all dogs bite . They start realizing and breaks down the or negative association. Not all Police hurt or not all people out there are bad.


Belinda Lamb is a group leader in the dog therapy program.
04:07

What makes this process so unique?

There are in the states a group doing the same and taking dogs into the court, I believe that we are the only group anywhere that actually dresses the role of the court. So everybody is identified with the role in the actual court. This helps the children because the process can take up to about 2 years before it gets to court





Claire V/O
16”






Father







Claire V/O
6”


Palesa




Sexual offences against children as in the case of convicted rapist Nicholas Ninow, who testified in mitigation of sentence this week, has a devastating effect on children and their families like one of the fathers that attended the the court preparation program.

What the children go through is very hard.
We didn't know that our child was being raped from 9 years old
He is on bail now , he is out and harassing .


__________________________________

15 Year old “Palesa” was viciously attacked by a perpetrator known to her __________________________________
I was assaulted when I was 14 years old. I was assaulted by my grandfathers girlfriend.
She assaulted my by pouring me with hot water and hitting me with a broomstick.
Claire V/O







Claire V/O
11”










Many children are left with short and long term psychological and behavioural problems




Desperate to find help for her and her daughter Thandi turned to the Teddy Bear Clinic for help.

03:38
She wasn't listening to me and she was just rebellious.
02;12
Like she’s got anger inside herself but wanted to show it out.

At the end of the day, you don’t know what the child wants, you don’t know what you have to do. So we came for counselling
Claire V/O
10”
But after all the counselling and preparation, it ends up in court where the already traumatized children have to face the harsh reality of the law.






Carina Coetzee
Senior Prosecutor, Sexual Offences Court
01:44
Children do feel anxious much quicker than adults, not knowing what they are going to encounter when they come to court causing severe trauma to children if they have to testify in open court


Claire V/O
5”
Carina Coetzee is a senior prosecutor in the National Prosecuting Authority.
Carina Coetzee




They have already been traumatized due to the offence , and to give evidence in that formal atmosphere as court and the way that we speak in court, off course causes a child immense trauma .if they have to testify in open court

Claire V/O
10”









Claire Link







Some children might even feel that participating in the Criminal Justice system is actually a punishment and that being part of the trial means that they are on trial.



There are numerous challenges when it comes to children having to testify in court, including the high levels of anxiety and the foreign environment, under these conditions children find it difficult to articulate themselves.









A child hops from one point to the next, they don’t have structure, they don’t have logic , they don't have flow when they tell a story. The perception is that if somebody jumps from one thing to the next, one part of the story to the other and jumps back and leaves out stuff, that they are not telling the truth. And to be able to give accurate, coherent , clear chronological evidence, its not possible




Claire V/O
8”







Child Witness Institute CEO Karen Hollily , is the co-author of a child witness preparation research project.
Karen Hollely

14:35
You also have to understand a child’s social development. Do they understand what has happened to them is wrong?
26:59
They don’t understand what is happening to them, They internalize this confusion, they internalise this fear. They internalize all of the feelings that they have while it’s happening , because they don’t understand.


Claire V/O
12”








Mbali
So, in helping children understand and work through the trauma of violence, animal assisted therapy, and conventional counselling have proven to be very successful in improving children’s confidence.



My experience with the dogs were very therapeutic . They really helped me, they made me feel more calm, There was no stress around them or fear of what is going to happen in the future.
Shaheda Omar







00:32
There is empirical
based evidence to support that by exposing children to furry animals , the touching and exposure creates a sense of wellbeing, the endorphins and it also reduces the stress hormones, the cortisol levels.

Belinda Lamb

03:05
We had a little girl, she has been coming for 5 or 6 months, no communication nothing, after the fourth visit there’s communication, she is smiling and she is interacting.


Belinda Lamb
Group Leader: Top Dogs








03:05
The child is hopefully starting to relax and eventually will start communicating with the people and therapist. And hopefully make the court process much more comfortable for them.
It’s very emotional for us.




Claire Question



03:45
But, are we doing enough in that court preparation currently, are there places perhaps where we could improve?



Carina Coetzee


03:45
Well, one always tries to develop, so I think is also where the animal assisted court preparations come in,it works well, it works very well. I remember that children were far worse witnesses than what they are now. If witnesses feel more at ease, they can contribute more positively to the trial.

Karen Hollely




O/Lay/ Archive : Witness testifying room
39:25

A child can participate effectively in the Criminal Justice system and it can be a good experience for them.
Mbali



When I appeared in court , and the first thing I thought of , Oh the dogs. The dogs really helped me understand more and I could actually make out who the person was but what they were wearing. I could understand who is on my side, who is not on my side.
Court Scene
I have no further questions, I close the state case.
